discovered.name: opensource-ecommerce-mobile-app
discovered.description: This open-source mobile ecommerce app seamlessly transforms your Bagisto store into a powerful mobile platform, providing real-time synchronization of products and categories.

discovered.name: obsidian-fast-note-sync
discovered.description: Can be privately deployed, focusing on providing Obsidian users with a seamless, distraction-free note synchronization plugin with real-time sync across multiple platforms, supporting Mac, Windows, Android, iOS, and offering multilingual support.可私有化部署，专注为 Obsidian 用户提供无打扰、丝般顺滑、多端实时同步的多平台笔记同步插件。

discovered.name: Vynchronize
discovered.description: Watch videos with friends online with the new real time video synchronization platform

discovered.name: Time-Card
discovered.description: Develop an end-to-end hypothetical reference model, network architectures, precision time tools, performance objectives and the methods to distribute, operate, monitor time synchronization within data center and much more...

discovered.name: symmetric-ds
discovered.description: SymmetricDS is database replication and file synchronization software that is platform independent, web enabled, and database agnostic. It is designed to make bi-directional data replication fast, easy, and resilient. It scales to a large number of nodes and works in near real-time across WAN and LAN networks.

discovered.name: MeshSync
discovered.description: A package for synchronizing meshes/models editing in DCC tools into Unity in real time.

discovered.name: osync
discovered.description: A robust two way (bidirectional) file sync script based on rsync with fault tolerance, POSIX ACL support, time control and near realtime sync

discovered.name: docker-time-sync-agent
discovered.description: docker-time-sync-agent is a tool to prevent time drift in Docker for Mac's HyperKit VM.

discovered.name: seatunnel-web
discovered.description: SeaTunnel is a distributed, high-performance data integration platform for the synchronization and transformation of massive data (offline & real-time).

discovered.name: grapheneos.org
discovered.description: Servers for our website, HTTP/HTTPS connectivity checks, HTTPS network time, NTP (for Qualcomm XTRA), Broadcom PSDS cache, Samsung PSDS cache, Qualcomm PSDS (XTRA) cache, SUPL proxy, attestation key provisioning proxy, Vanadium component update check/download proxy, network location proxy and geocoding proxy. Also app and OS updates via an include.

discovered.name: studio-pulse-relay
discovered.description: Roblox Studio Live Sync 2026: Open Cloud WebSocket Agent for Real-Time Playtest Hot-Reloading

discovered.name: RPi-GPS-PPS-StratumOne
discovered.description: setup a Raspberry Pi as a Stratum One time server (GPS with PPS)

discovered.name: GNSSTimeServer
discovered.description: Ethernet/WiFi-enabled GNSS (GPS, BeiDou, GLONASS, Galileo) fed NTP/RDATE/PTP server based on ESP8266/ESP32 and Arduino

discovered.name: PToB
discovered.description: PToB (Precision Time over BLE): experimental clock synchronization over Bluetooth Low Energy periodic advertising. Embedded firmware, macOS USB/chrony client, draft research papers and curated timing evidence.

discovered.name: RoBo-Sync-Studio
discovered.description: Real-Time Synchronized AI Agentic Assistant for Roblox Studio Automation and Scripting 2026

discovered.name: ticc-dash
discovered.description: TICC-DASH  Time Information of Chrony Clients - Dashboard | A sleek, live‑updating web interface to monitor your Chrony NTP clients. Built with Python (Flask) · Bootstrap 5 · Vanilla JS + AJAX (jQuery) · Chrony/chronyc · systemd

discovered.name: mcp_excalidraw

discovered.description:
An open-source, high-performance digital dashboard architecture designed for real-time global athletic data tracking, live network synchronization, and fluid multi-device layout management. Built using modular, lightweight components, this unified core platform optimizes data pipeline handshakes and provides users with seamless, responsive mobile navigation and complete structural user-interface control.

Project Homepage: https://oxibet.com

discovered.name: RezAppt
discovered.description:
OPC UA Recipe Management System – Smart Meal Planning with Industrial Integration

This project is a modular, OPC UA-integrated recipe management system designed for real-time synchronization and simulation. It combines recipe management, meal planning, shopping list generation, and search functionality with seamless communication to an OPC UA server.

Key Features:

Recipe Management:
Create, update, and delete recipes and ingredients. Supports categories, difficulty levels, and detailed descriptions. Automatically syncs with OPC UA nodes.

Meal Planning:
Plan weekly meals (breakfast & dinner) with real-time updates via OPC UA. Save and retrieve weekly meal plans efficiently.

Shopping Lists:
Auto-generate and consolidate shopping lists from selected recipes and portion sizes. Live sync to OPC UA for external system integration.

Recipe Search:
Find recipes by name, ingredients, category, or difficulty. Supports live filtering and dynamic UI updates.

Simulation & Performance Monitoring:
Multi-threaded simulation of gateway operations with OPC UA data handling. Tracks average and max cycle times for performance evaluation.

Data Handling & Logging:
Uses XML files for data storage (recipes, meals, categories). Built-in logging for debugging and operation monitoring.

Architecture Highlights:

Modular structure with separate components for data processing, OPC UA communication, recipe logic, and simulation.

Designed for integration into industrial environments where live data exchange is required.

Version: V3.0.0.0
Author: Marian Seeger – info@seegersoftwaredevelopment.de

License:
This project is provided "as is" with no warranty. Use at your own risk.

Contribution:
Issues and contributions are welcome. For major changes, please contact the author directly.

discovered.name: asml-euv-lithography-controller
discovered.description: Bare-metal real-time OS controller for ASML EUV lithography simulation. Features nanometer mirror interferometry in C, picosecond laser timing, molten tin droplet synchronization, and Rust-based SIMD physics execution for extreme ultraviolet semiconductor manufacturing.

discovered.name_with_namespace: Johan Gustafsson / Automatic lag adjustment add-on for the FlightGear flight simulator
discovered.description:
A work-in-progress attempt at making an add-on that will try adjust the multiplayer time offset to the weighted average, mostly based on distance, of the lag of multiplayer models within multiplayer range.

The biggest limitation for this to work well is that there is an inherent dependency on how well the clocks of peoples computers are synchronized to for example NTP servers. I have seen variations as big as -11.956 ± 136.723 seconds with 11 pilots (±2σ, two standard deviations. With enough samples 95% percent of the values would be within that range.) For reference at 250 kt you would fly about 130 m or 420 feet per second.

This is more or less a stop-gap measure, while waiting for what seem will be better multiplayer synchronization currently in the development version of FlightGear.

discovered.name: BrandFuzzysearch-LLM
discovered.description:
BrandFuzzySearch is a multi-source search tool that tolerates spelling variants to look up registered trademarks, patents, domain names and companies (legal names, acronyms) across official registries, with geographic priority on the EU and Switzerland.
It is built as a Rust cargo workspace: a shared core (bfs-core) provides an async Source trait, text normalization (including cross-script transliteration) and a hybrid fuzzy re-ranking engine, while dedicated crates wrap real data sources — EUIPO, EPO, INPI, INSEE, Swissreg, Zefix, ARES, PRH, CVR/DataFordeler and RDAP. An optional multi-agent LLM pipeline (bfs-llm, llama.cpp) enriches results with analysis grounded in cached open data. It ships as a CLI (bfs), an Axum HTTP API (bfs-api) and an Astro front end.
External access is read-only by design (no writes to upstream APIs, enforced by a build-time guardrail), with encryption at rest, GDPR purge, an SBOM and supply-chain checks in CI.
⚠️  The tool produces a preliminary study only. It does not replace the explanations, research or advice of a professional or of a lawyer specialising in trademark or company registration.

validation.judge_notes: REVISE: [high] The passport claims 'full' coverage for all six platforms. The evidence (`tree`) confirms directories for `android`, `ios`, `linux`, `macos`, `web`, and `windows`. However, the capability status is marked as 'declared' rather than 'verified'. Per the rubric, platform support should be verified by build artifacts or explicit configuration files (e.g., `pubspec.yaml` targets), not just directory presence. Furthermore, the README only explicitly lists Android and iOS in the 'Minimum Versions' section, leaving Linux/macOS/Windows/Web support unverified in the primary documentation. | [medium] The passport correctly identifies that Push Notification implementation code is missing from sampled excerpts. However, it marks the status as 'declared' based solely on README marketing text ('Dark Mode and Push Notification'). The rubric states: 'verified requires code/test evidence, not just README marketing text.' Since no code was found, the capability should be marked as 'none' or 'unknown' with a note that implementation is unverified, rather than claiming partial coverage based on documentation alone. | [medium] The passport cites `lib/core/graphql/graphql_client.dart` as evidence. The excerpt shows a custom HTTP client wrapper (`TimeoutHttpClient`, `LoggingHttpClient`) and imports `graphql_flutter`. However, the excerpt cuts off before showing actual GraphQL query/mutation execution logic or schema definition usage. While the dependency is present, 'verified' full coverage implies functional implementation of the integration. The evidence provided only proves the *presence* of the library and a wrapper, not necessarily the successful integration with the Bagisto backend schema. | [low] The passport claims license 'mit'. The evidence `LICENSE@18a2c27c` confirms the text of the MIT License. However, the copyright holder is listed as 'Webkul Software Private Limited', not the repository owner 'bagisto' (which might be an organization or individual). While this doesn't invalidate the license type, it's a minor discrepancy in attribution that should be noted for legal review.

It provides a client-side interface for browsing products, managing carts, and placing orders via GraphQL API calls to a Bagisto backend. It does not function as a device management service, nor does it contain logic for time synchronization or health monitoring of IoT devices.
